Glossary

Every "i" on this page explains one of these. The technical name is what the JSON and the older text report call it.

Branch coverage
The share of decision outcomes that can happen and that your tests took. It is the main number of this page. Technical name: branch coverage.
Decision outcome
One way a decision can go: an if being true or false, an activity succeeding or failing, one case of a switch, a wait ending by signal or by timeout. Technical name: branch, exit.
Grade
A word for the percentage: needs work below 60%, acceptable from 60%, commendable from 75%, exemplary from 90%. Your team can change the limits. Technical name: branches.grades.
Can be tested
A test can make the workflow take this route. Technical name: testable.
Can't happen
PathKit proved that nothing can make this happen, for example because an earlier value settles the decision. These outcomes are left out of the percentage and listed with the proof. Technical name: cannot-be-tested.
Needs a special test
It can happen in production but an ordinary test cannot reach it, for example the old side of a version check, which needs a replay of an old history. Technical name: needs-special-test.
Needs a person to check
PathKit is not sure. It stays in the numbers until a person decides. Technical name: needs-review.
Blocked by a known bug
A person marked this route as blocked by a bug that is known. It stays in the percentage, on a line of its own, until the bug is fixed. Technical name: known-defect.
Possible bug
The code tests for a plain value (a string, say) where the value is really a pointer to one, so the test can never be true. It is probably a mistake in the code, not a route that cannot happen. Technical name: likely-defect.
Two-step combinations
An outcome of one decision followed by an outcome of the next. A finer measure than branch coverage. Technical name: decision pairs.
Each part of a condition
In a condition like a && b, each part (a, b) should be seen true and false when it is checked. Technical name: condition coverage.
Tests notice wrong decisions
PathKit changed a decision to go the other way and ran the tests that cover it. This is how often a test failed. Technical name: decision check.
What to test next
The decision outcomes that can happen and that no test took, riskiest first. Technical name: tests to write first.
Risk
The riskiest thing a test of this outcome must do: cancel, undo (compensation), activity failure, continue as new, timer or timeout, signal or update, plain logic, or an old version. Technical name: tag.
Outcomes tested
How many of the outcomes that can happen your tests took, out of all of them. Technical name: branches covered / possible.
Missed
Outcomes that can happen and that no test took.
Test run
One run of a workflow recorded while your tests ran. Technical name: trace.
Test run PathKit couldn't place
A recorded run that does not fit any route PathKit drew. The drawing may be incomplete there, so PathKit trusts its "can't happen" proofs less around it. Technical name: unmatched trace.
Section of the workflow
A long workflow is cut into parts that are counted one at a time. Technical name: stage.
Scenario
A distinct list of things a workflow does outside itself (calls, timers, signals). Different routes that do the same things are one scenario. Technical name: scenario.
Path ID
A short code that names one route through a workflow and stays the same when unrelated code changes. Technical name: stableId.
Left out (can't happen)
Parts of a very large workflow that PathKit proved impossible and did not list one by one. They are counted exactly. Technical name: pruned groups.
Code PathKit couldn't read
Places PathKit did not follow, such as a call through an interface. A route through them has a scenario of its own and is never merged with another. Technical name: unread panel.
What PathKit assumes
Things PathKit takes for granted when it proves something can't happen, for example that Temporal's default JSON converter is used. Each can be turned off. Technical name: assumptions.
Path
One complete route through a workflow, from the start to an end. Technical name: path.
Workflow
One Temporal workflow function PathKit found.
Decision checklist
Every decision of a workflow in plain words, with each outcome ticked when a test took it, crossed when none did, or marked when it can't happen.
Possible bugs found
The places where the code looks like it tests a pointer as if it were the plain value. Technical name: likely-defect.
